summary: Each install now keeps itself on the sign-in and AI chat standard, the support heartbeat is never delayed by other work, and discovery handles two roles with the same name.

fixes.title: Sign-in standard applied by the update
fixes.text: Each update applies the sign-in standard to your install itself, including a long-lived session that renews on its own, and removes what the retired sign-in front left behind.

fixes.title: Status reports are never delayed
fixes.text: The report to support has its own slot, is sent right after an update, and only one full first run follows an update.

fixes.title: Roles with the same name
fixes.text: When two roles share a name, discovery gives each its own key and stores the role id, so approving gaps never creates a duplicate and the engine never guesses.

fixes.title: Stronger start-up check
fixes.text: The start-up check of Microsoft's token library also proves that an expired token is refused.

fixes.title: Smaller fixes
fixes.text: A refused change is judged once instead of on every run, the request API's app is pinned by its id, and AI chat settings can be set by the update.
